keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «가짜 뉴스는 진짜 뉴스인 것처럼 꾸민 거짓이거나 오해를 부르는 정보이다(주제)» 와 «정보가 넘치는 세상에서 가장 중요한 능력은 뉴스를 빨리 찾는 것이 아니라 꼼꼼히 판단하는 것이다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the topic (fake news is false or misleading information presented as real news) and the conclusion (the most important skill is not finding news quickly but judging it carefully). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why should we be especially careful when a headline makes us very angry or excited?
qs.qko: 헤드라인이 우리를 몹시 화나게 하거나 들뜨게 할 때 왜 특히 조심해야 하나요?
opts: Because strong emotions can stop us from thinking clearly
Because angry headlines are always written by bots
Because exciting stories are usually very old
evs: Some is created on purpose to make money from clicks or to influence opinions, while some spreads simply because people make mistakes.
Be especially careful when a headline makes you very angry or excited, since strong emotions can stop us from thinking clearly.
AI tools can now create realistic fake images, voices, and videos, sometimes called deepfakes.
Look carefully at the date, because old stories are often shared as if they were new.
why: 강한 감정은 우리가 분명하게 생각하지 못하게 막을 수 있기 때문이에요. 그래서 감정이 크게 흔들릴 때 더 조심해야 해요.
Strong emotions can stop us from thinking clearly, so we need to be extra careful.

qs.q: In the text, what does 'confirmation bias' mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 'confirmation bias(확증 편향)' 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: Checking a story with trusted news organizations
Sharing a story only after checking its date
Tending to believe information that matches what we already think
evs: Critical thinking means questioning information instead of accepting it immediately.
Fake news is false or misleading information presented as if it were real news.
Another reason is that we tend to believe information that matches what we already think, a habit called confirmation bias.
Before sharing a story, check who published it and whether trusted news organizations are reporting the same thing.
why: 이미 생각하고 있는 것과 맞는 정보를 믿는 습관을 confirmation bias 라고 부른다고 나와요.
The text says it is the habit of believing information that matches what we already think.

qs.q: Putting the two findings of the 2018 MIT study together, what can we learn?
qs.qko: 2018년 MIT 연구의 두 가지 결과를 합치면 무엇을 알 수 있나요?
opts: True news spreads faster, and bots spread most false stories
False news spreads faster, and people themselves are mainly responsible for spreading it
Twitter users never share stories they have not checked
evs: A large 2018 study of Twitter by researchers at MIT found that false news stories spread faster and reached more people than true ones.
AI tools can now create realistic fake images, voices, and videos, sometimes called deepfakes.
Surprisingly, the same study found that people, not automated bots, were mainly responsible for spreading the false stories faster.
Within minutes, thousands of people have shared it.
why: 한 결과는 거짓 뉴스가 진짜 뉴스보다 더 빨리, 더 많은 사람에게 퍼진다는 것이고, 다른 결과는 그것을 주로 퍼뜨린 것이 자동 봇이 아니라 사람이라는 것이에요. 둘을 합치면 우리의 선택이 중요하다는 걸 알 수 있어요.
One finding is that false news spreads faster and reaches more people; the other is that people, not bots, mainly spread it. Together they show that our own choices matter.
